co_moria.blurb: Moria is a small boulder cluster within the Sailing Hawks bouldering zone above Durango, centred on two enormous blocks that lean together to form a corridor with an upper and a lower chamber. Twelve problems are recorded, running from V0 up to V4, with most of the weight on V3 and V4 and just a few easier lines. Most of the lines sit in shade for much of the day. Landings are generally poor, so bring several pads and a partner who can spot. A short uphill walk on a distinct side trail from the main boulderfield brings you to it.

co_b_first_second_and_third_triangles.blurb: These three triangular slabs make up the heart of the Upper Tier of the Tiers of Zion, on the slopes above Lookout Mountain Road near Golden. The gneiss faces carry twelve routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a pair of gear routes and a couple of top-ropes. Grades cluster at 5.8 and 5.9, with a single 5.11, which makes the spot a good fit for newer leaders. Expect a steep hillside with scree and little flat ground at the base. The Third Triangle stands apart: reaching its base means a ramp scramble with a few short, exposed fourth-class moves.

co_cube_boulder.blurb: Cube Boulder is a blocky stone in the South Side area of Ute Valley Park in Colorado Springs, sitting east of the main boulder in the group. It holds twelve boulder problems across a wide spread: several easy lines around V0 to V2, a few mid-grade problems, and a handful of hard ones reaching V6 or V7. The best-known problems are a pair of Wedgie lines at the harder end of the mid-grades. This is a quick, low-commitment stop for a session rather than a full day, and it pairs well with the other blocks close by.

co_16z.blurb: 16Z is a remote sandstone crag in Colorado's far west, in the Naturita and Paradox Valley region. It lies in its own hanging valley above Big Gypsum Valley, so it can be windy. The twelve recorded climbs are mostly bolted sport routes, with a few boulder problems. Sport lines sit around 5.9 and 5.10, while the boulders stay between V0 and V2. The rock is highly featured and also offers crack climbing. Plan for a self-sufficient trip: it is a long way from any town.

co_big_wild_boulder.blurb: Big Wild Boulder is the largest and northernmost block in a small cluster in the Wild Rock area, high on Independence Pass between Aspen and Twin Lakes. It stands among trees, so it stays shaded through the day. Twelve climbs are recorded here: eight boulder problems from VB to V2, plus four hard bolted lines in the 5.12 to 5.13 range that feel like roped bouldering, with powerful moves from the ground up. Bring pads for the low problems and quickdraws for the sport lines.

co_bach_block_the.blurb: The Bach Block is a small sport-climbing sector at The Bank, one of the busiest parts of Shelf Road outside Canon City, where the rock is vertical limestone. Twelve bolted routes are recorded here, from about 5.7 to 5.10, and half of them fall in the 5.10 grades, so it suits climbers working through the moderate range. Three of its lines are favourites with other visitors. Because the sector sits in a popular zone, expect company on pleasant weekends.
